subject: Clarify default retention: EU residency + customer-controlled purge windows

2) Is there a supported customer-controlled purge window we can trigger (e.g., 30/45/90 days) from the Console or via API, and will that purge remove all KV/streamed buffers as well as persisted artifacts?

Hi Sara —

Short answers up front:
- Yes: For an EU-only tenancy we keep primary data residency in EU regions by default.
- Yes: Customers can request on-demand purges and configure default auto-purge windows; there are guardrails for auditability.

I want to give you the exact steps and constraints (and what "purge" covers) so I looped in Kimberly from our compliance team and Jonas who owns the private deployment flows. We'll reply with the precise Console/API flow and an implementation timeline for your SSO pilot.

Can you share the minimum retention window Evergreen needs as a hard requirement? That will help us surface any SLA/process notes.

Thanks,

Thanks, Avery.

Minimums:
- Residency: all request/response material (including prompts, streamed fragments, and final outputs) must remain in EU only. No telemetry or mirror copies in other regions.
- Purge window: we need ability to auto-expire to 45 days by default for non-production tenants, and to trigger immediate purge from the UI or an API endpoint for audit purposes.

Legal also attached a short SSO/audit snapshot they captured during the demo.

Sara

Subject: Re: Quick question on where logs live + purge options

Hi Sara —

Thanks for the specifics. I pulled together the exact behavior and constraints below so your security and legal teams have something to review. TL;DR: EU-only tenancy + 45-day auto-expire is supported; immediate purge is supported with caveats for audit evidence and backups.

What "EU-only tenancy" means in practice:
- Primary storage: All request/response artifacts (raw prompts, streamed fragments, final model outputs, and associated metadata) are stored in designated EU regions by default when the tenancy is provisioned as EU-only.
- Control plane: The control plane endpoints that manage tenancy configuration remain global, but control-plane logs do NOT contain request/response contents.
- Backups & replicas: We do not replicate request/response artifacts to non-EU regions for EU-only tenancies. Time-delayed backups (snapshots) remain in EU storage classes unless explicitly requested via an enterprise agreement.

Purge options and scope:
- Auto-expire windows: Customers can set tenancy-level auto-expire defaults (eg. 30/45/90 days) from the Console or via our Management API (PATCH /tenancies/{id}/retention).
- Immediate purge: An on-demand purge can be requested by the customer from the Console or by calling POST /tenancies/{id}/purge with justification. Purge removes: persisted output artifacts, request logs, KV cache entries written to persistent stores.
- Streaming snapshots: If you enable streaming transcript capture, transient buffers are flushed to persistent storage only when the session completes. Immediate purge removes completed session artifacts; for in-flight sessions we will truncate and mark them for removal once closed.

Auditability & evidence:
- Proof of deletion: When a purge runs we generate a signed deletion manifest (SHA256 checks) and a time-stamped audit record linked to the tenancy. That manifest is available via the Console and via API for compliance teams.
- Retention hold: Legal holds can be applied which suspend auto-expire and purge paths; applying a hold requires a recorded reason and an approver from the customer.

Caveats and exceptions:
- Third-party integrators: If Evergreen configures outbound integrations that mirror data (e.g., a third-party logging sink outside EU), Redwood cannot remove copies held by third parties. We will surface these integration paths during onboarding.
- Disaster recovery snapshots: For enterprise plans we offer cross-region disaster recovery; by default for EU-only customers this is off unless contractually enabled.

Next practical steps:
1) Avery — confirm the tenancy type you want provisioned for the pilot (EU-only).
2) Sara — if 45-day auto-expire is your default, we will stage the tenancy with that policy and provide the API calls you can use to trigger an immediate purge during pilot runs.
3) We will add the signed deletion manifest example to the Drive folder you shared.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call if you want to walk through the Console flows.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Director, Compliance & Privacy, Redwood Inference

Hi all —

Quick operational notes from the Private deployment side:
- Provisioning ETA: EU-only tenancy for a pilot (single-tenant VPC) can be provisioned in ~5 business days after contract sign-off.
- API semantics: POST /tenancies/{id}/purge runs an async job; response includes job_id and estimated completion. We will emit a deletion manifest once the job finishes.
- Validation: We'll provide a validation script you can run post-purge that checks for presence of known test markers (we'll coordinate a small test dataset).

Avery — I can join the call if you schedule it.

Thanks,
